title: The Chai Wars Come to New York: How Two Bengali Brothers and a Comedian Are Taking On Starbucks
excerpt: Kolkata Chai Co. just landed a Michelin-starred backer in Vikas Khanna, adding to Hasan Minhaj's earlier investment — and the $10 billion masala chai market is paying attention.
body:
There is a specific kind of heartbreak familiar to every Indian who has ever ordered a "chai tea latte" in America and received a lukewarm cup of cinnamon-flavored milk. Ani and Ayan Sanyal know it well. The Bengali-American brothers grew up in Massachusetts, spending summers in Kolkata sipping roadside chai — the real kind, brewed strong with ginger, cardamom and black tea, served in terracotta cups that you smash when you are done.

In 2019, they decided to fix the problem. Kolkata Chai Co. opened as a 100-square-foot café in New York's East Village with a single mission: authentic Indian masala chai, unapologetically brewed the way their grandmother made it. On opening day, after DMing every follower they had on social media, 800 people showed up.

## From a Tiny Café to a National Brand

Seven years later, Kolkata Chai operates multiple café locations in Manhattan, sells chai blends and concentrates through its own channels and Amazon, and has built a community that treats the brand less like a beverage company and more like a cultural movement.

"We felt like our own culture and all the beautiful aspects of where we came from — the food, the culture of the community — were being left out of conversation in the Western world," Ani Sanyal told *Imbibe* magazine earlier this year. "There weren't any third spaces that were reflective of not only authentic chai, but what this first-gen experience looked like."

The brand's growth has attracted serious attention. In 2024, comedian, actor and *Patriot Act* host Hasan Minhaj joined as an investor and business partner, calling it an opportunity to give chai its "matcha moment." Speaking to *ADWEEK*, Minhaj was blunt: "This wasn't another perfunctory celebrity ambassadorship." He wanted skin in the game.

## Enter the Michelin-Starred Chef

This weekend, the stakes rose again. Bungalow Hospitality Investments — a new platform co-founded by Michelin-starred chef Vikas Khanna and restaurateur Jimmy Rizvi — announced a strategic investment in Kolkata Chai Co. The deal includes an exclusive menu integration: Kolkata Chai's signature masala chai will be served across Bungalow Hospitality's New York restaurants, including GupShup and the upcoming Punjab Meet House.

"To have him join the Kolkata Chai family is a genuinely exciting moment," Minhaj said of Khanna's arrival.

For the Sanyal brothers, having both a TIME 100 chef and an Emmy-winning comedian in their corner validates years of grinding. But the real validation may be in the numbers. According to Verified Market Research, the global masala chai market exceeded $5.4 billion in 2023 and is projected to approach $10 billion by 2031, driven by health consciousness, café culture and social media — TikTok chai-making videos routinely rack up hundreds of thousands of views.

## The Diaspora's Drink

The chai conversation is deeply personal for NRIs. It is the first thing your mother makes when you walk through the door. It is what you miss at 4 p.m. in a conference room in San Francisco. And for a long time, the American version — overly sweet, vaguely spiced, served from a pump — felt like a small cultural erasure.

Kolkata Chai and a growing cohort of authentic chai brands are changing that. The product line now includes concentrates, loose-leaf blends and ready-to-drink options that let Americans taste what chai actually is, rather than what Starbucks decided it should be.

"Food is an incredible way to share culture," Ayan Sanyal has said. "Kolkata Chai Co. is where our two homes finally meet: a space that celebrates the duality of the immigrant experience and the comfort of connection in every cup."

With a Michelin-starred chef, a celebrity comedian and a $10 billion market behind them, the Sanyal brothers' bet on authenticity is looking increasingly like the smart money.
